Article Title: UPI charges: Lok Sabha passes bill for government to make changes
Article Text:
The FM said the charge will apply to merchants and not to users and will help banks and fintech invest in infrastructure and innovation

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Lok Sabha on Thursday passed a Bill that seeks to ease tax rules to attract investments and remove the existing legal provision that prevents banks and payment service providers from charging Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on notified electronic payment modes.The Bill — passed without discussion amid din — also proposes to remove the linkage between the Payment and Settlement Systems Act and the I-Tax Act and give legal backing to the government to modify the zero-MDR framework on UPI and RuPay card transactions. Outside the House, however, there was an exchange between FM Nirmala Sitharaman and Congress MP Jairam Ramesh. Ramesh said the Bill opens the doors for MDR. The FM responded, saying the charge will apply to merchants and not to users and will help banks and fintech invest in infrastructure and innovation.“More importantly, the UPI and services steering committee headed by NPCI is yet to decide on the MDR. This will happen after Parliament passes the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026... All this could have been discussed on the floor of the House if your party @INCIndia (Congress) engages constructively in Parliament when the Bill was/is tabled,” she said.While leaving person-to-payments outside MDR’s ambit, banks and fintechs may be permitted to charge 0.25% to 0.4% on payments to businesses in excess of Rs 2,000 with an overall ceiling on how much can be charged.Officials have argued that the levy will be lower than what is charged on credit and debit cards, and most merchants will not pass it on to consumers.
Article Summary: The bill also proposes to remove the linkage between the payment and settlement systems act and the i-tax act. Outside the house, there was an exchange between fm nirmala sitharaman and congress mp jairam ramesh. The fm said the charge will apply to merchants and not to users.

Article Title: Netanyahu calls PM Modi, discusses bilateral ties, West Asia situation
Article Text:
The affirmation of friendship comes at a time of Israel losing supporters over Netanyahu’s military offensive in retaliation for Hamas’s terror attack

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday received a telephone call from his Israeli counterpart Benjamin Netanyahu, with the two reviewing progress on various facets of both countries' special strategic partnership and also exchanging views on the current situation in West Asia.PM Modi posted on X that India-Israel Special Strategic Partnership continues to go from strength to strength. "The two reviewed sustained progress in the special strategic partnership and reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening the bilateral cooperation across various sectors for the mutual benefit of both countries," said the government in a statement.The affirmation of friendship comes at a time when Israel has lost many of its traditional supporters and sympathisers because of Netanyahu's military offensive in retaliation to Hamas's terror attack on its civilian population. Significant sections in the US, Israel's principal backer, have soured on the country, while there is growing support for the Palestinian cause. PM Modi had visited Israel days before Israel and the US attacked Iran: a coincidence which has been cited by the opposition to accuse the government of a tilt towards Netanyahu.In his address to the Israeli Parliament, PM Modi had declared that India would stand with Israel in the latter's fight against terrorism.Criticism does not appear to have deterred the government from strengthening ties with Israel, which has emerged as a source of sophisticated weaponry and help in times of conflict. "Netanyahu and PM Modi also exchanged views on the developments in West Asia," it added.

Article Title: 15 Indian seafarers killed in West Asia and Black Sea conflicts: Regulator
Article Text:
Following shipping minister's directions, DGMA has put in place a mechanism to track every Indian seafarer operating in high-risk water

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Conflicts in West Asia and the Black Sea have claimed the lives of 15 Indian seafarers, while two remain missing in 57 separate incidents over the past three months, India’s maritime regulator, Directorate General of Maritime Administration (DGMA), said on Thursday, describing the current geopolitical situation as “extremely challenging”.Addressing the National Port Security Conference in the capital, DGMA Shyam Jagannathan said drone and missile attacks on defenceless merchant vessels had become rampant in parts of the Black Sea. “Piracy off the coast of Somalia is reappearing. The Houthi security threat, which accounted for more than 154 incidents in 2024, has resurfaced,” he said.Jagannathan said the conflicts had significantly increased global logistics costs. He said since the end of Feb, the DGMA has been in an extremely high state of alert.The regulator said it had strengthened coordination for rescue operations, vessel movements and issuance of advisories, while ensuring compliance with best management practices for piracy response, validation of citadel preparedness and coordination among multiple security agencies.Following directions from shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal, the DGMA has also put in place a mechanism to track every Indian seafarer operating in high-risk waters, making the administration accountable for their safety, security and early repatriation.Speaking at the conference, Sonowal said as India’s maritime footprint expands, “the responsibility to secure it also grows”.“A modern port cannot be judged only by its capacity, efficiency or turnaround time. It must also be judged by how safe, secure and resilient it is. Cyber threats, drones, supply chain disruptions and risks to digital networks, information systems and critical infrastructure have added entirely new dimensions to maritime security,” he said, adding that the guiding principle should be “security by design”.Later in the day, commenting on the evolving geopolitical situation, another senior DGMA official said Russia’s response in the Black Sea had become “more severe”.
Article Summary: Conflicts in west asia and the black sea have claimed the lives of 15 indian seafarers. Two remain missing in 57 separate incidents over the past three months. Dgma has put in place a mechanism to track every indian seafarer operating in high-risk water.

Article Title: Gen Z more honest, protesters not anti-national: Bhagwat
Article Text:
RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat at an interaction with 'Gen Z' in Mumbai

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Calling Gen Z and Gen Alpha more "honest" than adults RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat on Thursday rejected attempts to brand protesting youngsters "anti-national," and said they have "an honest feeling of patriotism." He described protest as a legitimate form of democratic dialogue and said their questions must be answered with logic, affection and a sense of belonging.By the end of the freewheeling exchange, the 75-year-old had also picked up a new expression from his young audience — “clock it” — and tried it out before the cheering crowd, adding a lighter finish to a conversation that ranged from student protests and reservation to social media, LGBTQ rights and relations with Pakistan and China.The interaction, held as part of IIMUN’s 15th anniversary celebration in Mumbai, was driven by questions from Gen Z and Gen Alpha delegates on issues ranging from education and jobs to reservation, social media and the right to protest.“I feel that this new generation — Gen Z and Gen Alpha — is more honest than our existing generation. There is an honest feeling of patriotism and service in them,” Bhagwat said, adding, “They are not anti-national.They are our own people, our next generation,” . The exchange came against the backdrop of recent Gen Z-led protests over examination irregularities, education and jobs.Bhagwat said young people today were unlike earlier generations that often accepted what elders told them without question. “They ask questions. They want logical answers, and along with that, they want affection,” he said.“I feel this new generation — Gen Z and Gen Alpha — is more honest than our existing generation. The honest impulse of patriotism and service is stronger in them,” he added.Bhagwat said protest should not be treated as the opposite of dialogue. “Protest is also a way of dialogue,” he said, describing it as a democratic means of building consensus. An agitation, he added, should seek to correct the system rather than target individuals or deepen divisions.Asked about allegations of lathi-charge and pellet firing on young protesters, Bhagwat said he did not have enough verified information to reach a conclusion. “I place my trust in Gen Z,” he said.Bhagwat backed the longstanding demand to allocate 6% of the Budget to education, saying, “The demand is justified. It should be implemented.” He also argued that education should not be treated as a commercial business.Turning to social media, Bhagwat warned against trusting content without checking authentic sources, particularly when technology could produce fake images, voices and videos. Influencers and public figures, he said, must recognise their responsibility because lakhs of people may imitate them.Turning to affirmative action, he said reservation must continue as long as social discrimination remained. “Those who have received its benefit and whose condition has improved should give up that benefit for others,” he said. Bhagwat also referred favourably to sub-categorisation so that the benefits reached those still left behind, and blamed politics for creating “bad blood” over a measure intended to promote social unity.The discussion also moved to LGBTQ rights. Bhagwat said the community was part of society and must be accommodated, but favoured wider debate on a legal framework for same-sex companionship rather than an immediate change to the institution of marriage.He also said people-to-people relations with Pakistan and China could be paused during war or terrorism but should not be permanently severed. “Permanent enmity is not the solution,” he said.The discussion also turned to jobs, with Bhagwat arguing that employment should not be reduced to salaried or government work. Entrepreneurship, skilled work and self-employment were equally valid, he said, calling for the restoration of "shram pratishtha", or dignity of labour. Society, he added, must stop ranking occupations as high or low and accord equal respect to anyone earning honestly, whether through farming, manual work, private employment, government service or a small enterprise.Asked why the RSS remained a male organisation despite describing women as equal partners in nation-building, Bhagwat said men and women were “equal and complementary” and should receive the same training and opportunities. He said the Rashtra Sevika Samiti functioned independently with the RSS’s support, while women working in public organisations were invited to the Akhil Bharatiya Pratinidhi Sabha and participated in its decision-making process. He also indicated that organisational integration could be considered if the women’s organisation itself sought it.
Article Summary: Rss chief mohan bhagwat rejects attempts to brand protesting youngsters 'anti-national' he described protest as a legitimate form of democratic dialogue. The 75-year-old picked up a new expression from his young audience — “clock it” rashtra sevika samiti functioned independently with the rss’s support.

Article Title: 'Grievance of Gen Z genuine': RSS chief defends protest as way of 'reaching consensus' in democracy
Article Text:
RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat said "protest is a way of dialogue".

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat Thursday strongly backed the students who were protesting against NEET irregularities, saying that the "grivances of the Gen Z is genuine".Calling "protest is a way of dialogue", the Sangh supremo said: "I won’t say that Gen Z should not protest, but in a democracy there are ways of going about it ... I'm saying, if Gen Z is protesting, they're not anti-national. They're our own people. They're our next generation. With this sense of belonging, along with dialogue, I said a sense of belonging is needed. A relationship is needed. That is our relationship. Its recognition is needed. "The RSS chief further said that Gen Z and Gen Alpha want "logical answers" to the questions raised by them.He also said that the "education is not a commercial business", arguing that it should be "structured in such a way that it is available for all" and that "society should also contribute to improving status of education".Earlier, Bhagwat urged parents to lead by example instead of blaming the younger generation, saying many of the challenges children face today stem from adults' own behaviour.Speaking at a programme on "Motherhood in the Current Era" organised by Vishwa Mangalya Sabha, Bhagwat said Gen Z is emotional, imitative and responds to what it perceives as genuine.He also observed that today's youth view authority figures as equals or friends, adding that questioning authority has always been a part of adolescence. Families, he said, should encourage teamwork and open communication instead of confrontation.When asked about incidents during protests where young people were allegedly subjected to lathi charges and pellet gun firing, Bhagwat said he didn't have complete information but if he had to pick a side, he would place his faith in Gen Z."Regarding such matters, we need to first understand what happened and why it happened. We need to examine the reasons behind it. I do not have all the information required to give a complete opinion on this issue, and I do not think you have the complete details either.We need to look into where exactly the problem lies," he said.Further he added: "At this moment, I cannot say what happened or who was right or wrong, because I do not have complete information. You are sharing what you have read, and I am also going by what I have read... However, if I am asked to place my faith in someone, I would place my faith in Gen Z."
Article Summary: Rss chief mohan bhagwat said "protest is a way of dialogue" he said that gen z and gen alpha want "logical answers" to the questions raised by them. He urged parents to lead by example instead of blaming the younger generation.

The Meta row continued on Thursday as the company’s global team held further discussions with the government over compliance with Indian laws, a day after the company apologised for briefly removing a video posted by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.Meta’s global team is expected to remain in India for another three to four days, with more meetings planned with government officials, with the discussions also expected to cover WhatsApp issues. Meanwhile, the talks with IT ministry officials continued for a 2nd day during which the IT giant admitted to 'serious issues' and assured that they are "working hard" over CSAM, deepfakes & bots issues, as per PTI sources.The government is seeking details on Meta’s algorithms, content moderation, compliance mechanisms, checks and balances and safeguards, including the systems used to tackle child sexual abuse material (CSAM) and deepfake content.“Platforms can't be run in India as per US law. Joel Kaplan, Meta’s chief global affairs officer, said he had apologised to Vaishnaw “on behalf of Meta for the error restricting PM Modi’s post”. The government had also raised concerns over CSAM, deepfake content and Meta’s content moderation systems.The government has further questioned Meta’s compliance with Indian laws and its eligibility for safe-harbour protection under Section 79 of the Information Technology Act, which provides intermediaries protection from liability for third-party content subject to certain conditions.

Article Title: On the frontlines: How Indian sailors are paying the price in Middle East war
Article Text:
10 Indian sailors have been killed in the Middle East while hundreds are still sailing the dangerous waters

Numbers tell the story

An officer died as he got sick on vessel off Oman Coast

The silent toll on India

The cost of war that India has paid

‘Seafarers are not warriors’

Life on board

While world powers engage in military blockades and political posturing, the people suffering the real humanitarian crisis are the innocent seafarers trapped onboard. Deepak Kumar, third officer in merchant navy

Every seafarer should have the right to decline sailing through a high risk area without fear of damaging their career. Amit Khareta, MD at Barrow & Trent Shipping India

Protecting sailors

Cost of trade

For thousands of Indian merchant seafarers, the Middle East war has transformed the sea from a workplace into a battlefield.They are not soldiers. They are civilians who keep global trade moving, transporting oil, fuel and essential cargo through some of the world's busiest shipping lanes, including the Strait of Hormuz, the Gulf of Oman and the Red Sea. But since the US-Israel war with Iran erupted on February 28, many have found themselves navigating through missile strikes, drone attacks and naval hostilities.Some never made it home. Indian sailors have been killed in attacks on commercial vessels. Others have been injured or stranded at sea for weeks, unable to escape the conflict. Back home, anxious families spend their days glued to news bulletins, fearing every report of another ship being struck and praying for a phone call confirming their loved ones are still alive.The scale of the crisis is stark.The ministry of external affairs (MEA) recently said 166 Indian seafarers remained in the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz region, with 125 aboard six Indian-flagged vessels and another 41 serving on foreign ships. In an update on August 4, the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways said 3,972 Indian seafarers had been repatriated from the Gulf region, underscoring the massive effort to bring them out of one of the world's most dangerous conflict zones.India is the world's second-largest supplier of seafarers after the Philippines, with 311,936 personnel accounting for 12.16 per cent of the global maritime workforce, according to the BIMCO-ICS Seafarer Workforce Report 2026.Indian officers make up 13.41 per cent of the world's officer workforce, while the country also supplies 171,218 ratings, representing 11.29 per cent of the global ratings workforce.That vast presence at sea has come at a heavy cost since the Iran war erupted.Last month, the MEA said Indian seafarers had suffered the highest number of fatalities of any nationality in attacks on commercial shipping. Later, the government informed Parliament that 10 Indian seafarers were among the 16 Indian nationals killed in the Middle East conflict.However, the human cost extends far beyond those killed in missile and drone attacks.Hundreds of Indian sailors stranded in conflict-hit waters have faced prolonged deployments, delayed crew changes, disrupted medical evacuations, supply shortages and worsening onboard conditions, exposing them to mounting physical and mental risks.One such tragedy unfolded in June when 35-year-old Second Officer Nishanth Uirthanathan died from medical complications aboard the MT Celestial near Oman after falling seriously ill.The Indian Embassy coordinated the repatriation of his remains, while the Federation of Seafarers' Unions of India (FSUI) alleged that critical medical assistance was delayed because the vessel was operating in a conflict zone. Following his death, crew members reportedly had to preserve his body using bottles of cold water as the ship lacked adequate refrigeration facilities.The human cost for India was almost immediate.Within 24 hours of the Iran war erupting, Indian seafarers had begun paying the price.On March 1. Captain Ashish Kumar and crew member Dalip (Daleep) Singh were killed when the Palau-flagged tanker Skylight was attacked near Oman's Musandam Peninsula. Hours later, another Indian seafarer lost his life after the Marshall Islands-flagged gasoline tanker MKD Vyom was struck off the Omani coast.The attacks continued over the following months.On March 11, 54-year-old Deonandan Prasad Singh was killed when the Marshall Islands-flagged Safesea Vishnu came under fire near Basra, Iraq.On May 8, Indian seafarer Altaf Talab Ker died and four others were injured after the Indian-flagged dhow Al Faize Noor Suleimani was caught in crossfire in the Strait of Hormuz.The single deadliest attack came on June 10, when the Palau-flagged Settebello was struck by US forces in the Gulf of Oman, killing Chief Engineer Patnala Suresh, Deck Cadet Aditya Sharma and Fitter Shivanand Chaurashiya.The toll continued to climb in July.Marine engineer Herambh Karmarkar was killed on July 12 after the Cyprus-flagged GFS Galaxy was hit shortly after transiting the Strait of Hormuz. Ten of the vessel's 11 Indian crew members were rescued.Two days later, Indian seafarer Rohan Kumar was killed when the Liberia-flagged Mombasa B was struck by Iranian missiles alongside Al Bahyah in Omani waters.Together, the two vessels carried 30 Indian seafarers.Other India-linked vessels also came under attack but avoided fatalities. The cargo ship Haji Ali was hit on May 13, while Marivex and Jalveer were attacked in June, with all Indian crew members rescued.The violence has shown little sign of easing.On August 4, the Indian-flagged MSV Faize Noore Oliya was hit near Yemen and sank. All 13 Indian crew members survived, narrowly escaping what could have been another deadly addition to India's mounting toll.For merchant seafarers, the risks are fundamentally different: commercial vessels can become targets, crews can be stranded for days and even routine medical emergencies can become life-threatening when ports and evacuation routes are disrupted.That has put a new question at the centre: who protects the people onboard?Recently, the sinking of the Indian-flagged MSV Faize Noore Oliya on 4 August has intensified calls for stronger protection of merchant crews. The Federation of Seafarers' Unions of India (FSUI), one of the key seafarer bodies advocating for their safety, has asked PM Modi to deploy Navy assets to protect Indian-flagged ships and Indian crews across the Hormuz, the Red Sea and the Black Sea.The Navy already operates Urja Suraksha, an escort mission for energy shipments through the Strait. FSUI wants such protection extended to commercial vessels and says it had warned the government about the risks in the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait roughly a month before the Faize Noore Oliya attack.Raising concerns on safety, FSUI general secretary Manoj Yadav told TOI. “Today’s escalation of war, which has reached the sea from land, targets commercial vessels from either side — the US and Iran,” adding that crews, including large numbers of Indians, are being caught in a conflict they had no role in.Yadav argued that military or naval forces can stop a commercial vessel without harming its crew; by boarding or detaining it, for instance instead of targeting sensitive areas such as engine rooms and accommodation blocks.“Seafarers are not warriors. They work to serve the nation and the global supply chain,” Yadav reiterated.FSUI's concerns extend beyond attacks. It says thousands of seafarers remain at risk in the Persian Gulf and Black Sea, while war-risk insurance gaps can leave families without compensation. The union has called for a government-backed insurance mechanism, $5 million for each deceased seafarer's family and employment support for next of kin.FSUI has also urged the government to seek a UN-backed independent inquiry into the deaths of seafarers in conflict zones and establish accountability.“Seafarers are the heartbeat of the ocean,” Yadav said. FSUI has called on seafarers both aboard ships and ashore to observe September 25 as a Day of Global Maritime Mourning.For the people actually on ships, the war is not a headline, it's a watch schedule.Deepak Kumar, a Third Officer in the Merchant Navy, said shipping companies now run detailed risk assessments and add security measures before entering high-risk waters, and depending on the threat level, some deploy armed guards while naval forces patrol the surrounding sea.But no amount of planning removes the strain."No seafarer wants to sail through a high-risk maritime zone," as every transit means disturbed sleep, patchy contact with home, and having to "put your emotions aside" and keep the ship running regardless.Kumar added that the hardest part often isn't the danger itself but the silence around it: families hearing of an attack near their loved one's trading route and waiting for a message confirming they're safe.Ritik Raina, another Third Officer, explained why the Hormuz transit is uniquely brutal.There is a distinction between a High Risk Area, where seafarers face threats such as piracy and armed attacks, and a Warlike Operations Area, where they are exposed directly to an ongoing military conflict. The latter carries far greater implications for crews, including enhanced compensation and, under international maritime labour agreements, the right to refuse to enter the area, he explained.The Strait of Hormuz was initially designated a High Risk Area on March 2, before being upgraded to a Warlike Operations Area three days later.For crews already inside the Gulf, however, the geography makes that distinction consequential.The Gulf is enclosed on three sides, with the Strait of Hormuz as its only maritime exit.“Once a ship is inside the Gulf, it simply cannot leave until the blockade lifts, leaving crews to ration food, watch fresh water systems run down, and lose internet access as onboard connectivity, decided by shipowners, thins out or disappears,” said Raina.Contracts do carry war-zone bonuses, he further explained, and sailors can refuse to sail into a designated danger area before a vessel enters it.Meanwhile, former chief engineer and managing director at Barrow & Trent Shipping India Amit Khareta said geopolitical risk is increasingly becoming a reality the shipping industry has to plan around. Larger companies can sometimes divert via the Cape of Good Hope, but the added cost is not always practical for smaller owners, who may continue using high-risk routes after risk assessments and taking additional war-risk insurance.For seafarers, the choice is complicated.Khareta said many crews he has spoken to are willing to sail.Higher war-risk bonuses and additional compensation also influence that decision, with some owners offering several times the normal salary for such voyages.While Khareta himself has chosen not to sail through the current danger zone because of family obligations, he said he understands why experienced seafarers do it. But the decision, he stressed, must remain voluntary; “every seafarer should have the right to decline sailing through a high-risk area without fear of damaging their career.”The bigger burden, he said, is often psychological. Families worry constantly, seafarers face enormous pressure themselves while longer routes, disrupted schedules and fatigue add to the strain, but the uncertainty of not knowing what may happen once a ship enters a conflict zone weighs most heavily. “Merchant seafarers are civilians,” Khareta said. “They are not part of the conflict, yet they are exposed to its consequences simply because global trade depends on them. ”Beyond the decisions made by individual seafarers and shipping companies, the crisis has also put the spotlight on the systems meant to protect shipping in conflict zones.International maritime law already provides several layers of protection.The Maritime Labour Convention, 2006 sets minimum standards for seafarers' working and living conditions, including wages, medical care, repatriation and welfare. SOLAS lays down safety requirements for ships, while the ISPS Code deals specifically with ship and port security, requiring vessels to assess security risks and maintain plans and procedures to respond to them. But these rules were not designed to make merchant ships immune to an active war.In this context, Vidhu Shekhar, associate professor at SPJIMR, brought an economic lens to the problem, particularly on how maritime risk is distributed between shipowners, insurers and crews.“Routing decisions are made principally by owners and charterers, while the physical risk is borne by crews who have little influence over those decisions,” Shekhar said. He said sharper protections such as hazard pay and refusal rights have therefore often come through collective agreements, leaving some seafarers facing the same danger without equivalent protection. “Risk is therefore priced by contractual coverage rather than consistently by the hazard itself,” he added.For Indian sailors, Shekhar said the exposure is particularly unusual because most Indians serving internationally work aboard foreign-flagged vessels, making protection dependent on coordination between India, flag states, shipowners and insurers.India has meanwhile strengthened its own safety net. The government's ‘Seafarer-First’ framework includes real-time tracking of vessels and Indian crews, a 24-hour control room, coordination with the Indian Navy and voyage-specific risk assessments.Government advisories have also directed shipping companies and licensed Recruitment and Placement Services (RPSL) agencies to avoid deploying Indian seafarers on voyages through the Strait of Hormuz during periods of heightened risk.Meanwhile, for Upasha Kumari, a researcher on India's SAGAR doctrine, the bigger problem is that the human cost remains secondary to discussions around shipping.“We often discuss oil prices and shipping routes, but rarely the people operating those ships,” she said. “Indian seafarers are on the frontlines of these crises.” As commercial routes increasingly overlap with conflict zones, she argued that protecting civilian crews must become a central part of maritime security and not an afterthought.For India, the challenge is not only keeping its seafarers out of danger, but ensuring that those who keep global trade moving are not left to bear the cost of conflicts they did not choose.They are civilians, working far from home, often on vessels whose routes and risks they do not control.As the war pushes commercial shipping deeper into contested waters, the question is no longer simply how to keep the cargo moving. It is how to make sure the people carrying it can make it home.
Article Summary: 10 indian sailors have been killed in the middle east while hundreds are still sailing the dangerous waters. India is the world's second-largest supplier of seafarers after the philippines, with 311,936 personnel accounting for 12.16 per cent of the global maritime workforce.

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) said on Thursday that they will continue to function as a public pressure group instead of entering electoral politics for now, after a two-day meeting of the organisation's core team in Maharashtra's Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.Addressing a press conference after the meeting, its founder Abijeet Dipke said CJP would focus on building a nationwide citizens' movement around issues including unemployment, education, transparency, accountability and institutional reforms. NEW DELHI: Air India's recent severe turbulence incident is now under a "thorough investigation" by the directorate general of civil aviation (DGCA), civil aviation minister Ram Mohan Naidu said on Wednesday.Naidu said the Air India flight from Phuket to New Delhi experienced severe turbulence for "four to five minutes", leaving several passengers injured and some crew members with spinal and neck injuries.At least 17 people, including four cabin crew members, were injured after the aircraft suddenly lost around 300 feet in altitude during the midair turbulence.Addressing the media, Naidu said the aircraft was secured immediately after landing and all crucial evidence has been taken into the regulator's custody."In terms of why the incident has happened, we have immediately alerted the DGCA to thoroughly investigate the situation. The moment the plane was landed, it was put in a separate hangar. The data recorder, the voice recorder, everything is in the possession of DGCA. They will thoroughly investigate how and why this incident happened. Only when we have the facts in front of us, we are going to make it public," he said.The minister said medical teams attended to passengers and crew immediately after the flight landed in Delhi."The moment the flight landed in Delhi, the medical assistance team immediately attended to them. All first aid and medical assistance that needed to be provided was done at the airport itself. There were some passengers and crew members who were observed to need more medical assistance, they were shifted to Medanta Hospital and also Fortis Hospital," Naidu added.He said seven passengers admitted to Medanta Hospital on Monday were discharged after undergoing medical examinations."Spinal Injuries Centre, Fortis Centre - two passsengers were admitted yesterday. They both were also discharged but four crew members were admitted in Fortis where I also personally visited along with Ministry Team and DGCA Team. We interacted with crew members also. They have been very brave, even after that incident happened for 5 minutes and they were prone to certain injuries, the plane had to travel for 1 more hour. Even through that hour, the crew members provided all the assistance that was required. So, it was very brave of the women, the crew members who were on the flight," he said.The Airbus A320neo, operating as flight AI2379 from Phuket to Delhi on Tuesday, was carrying 137 passengers and eight crew members. Following the turbulence, 13 passengers and four crew members sustained injuries and were taken to hospitals for medical evaluation.According to Air India, as of 6:50 pm, five passengers had been discharged, while the remaining injured continued to receive treatment and care.An Air India spokesperson said on Tuesday, "Earlier today, Air India flight AI2379 operating from Phuket to Delhi experienced a sudden loss of altitude during cruise. After the momentary event, the aircraft continued normally and landed safely in Delhi at 11:07 hrs IST."The DGCA is now investigating the incident to determine the cause of the severe midair turbulence.

Article Title: 'Biggest attack since World War II': What stopped massive US strike on Iran? Trump reveals
Article Text:
Trump maintained that while he remains open to diplomacy

US President Donald Trump said that the United States was on the verge of launching what he described as the "biggest attack since World War II" on Iran before Tehran reached out to seek talks. He claimed that the prospect of a massive military strike pushed Iran back to the negotiating table.Speaking at an event in Las Vegas on Wednesday, Trump said Iranian officials contacted him just before the planned operation. "They called me and they said, 'Please don't do it, let's talk,'" Trump told supporters, presenting the outreach as a result of sustained US military pressure.Trump maintained that while he remains open to diplomacy, Washington's position on Iran's nuclear ambitions has not changed. "I'd rather make a deal because I don't want to kill people," he said. "But Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon."His remarks came as the Trump administration signalled that negotiations over reopening the Strait of Hormuz were nearing a breakthrough. Trump said on Tuesday that "a lot of progress" had been made and suggested an agreement could be announced "tomorrow or the next day".Iran also indicated that talks were advancing. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said Tehran and Oman were in the "final stage" of drafting an agreement on the strategically vital waterway and that a joint statement could follow if "certain parties do not obstruct this process".According to regional officials cited by the Associated Press, Iranian and Omani negotiators have finalised a draft agreement and are awaiting approval from Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei. The proposed deal is reportedly intended as a temporary arrangement that could pave the way for renewed US-Iran nuclear negotiations.However, major differences remain. Iran has insisted on retaining a degree of control over the Strait of Hormuz, while the US has rejected any agreement that would allow Tehran to charge transit fees or strengthen its hold over one of the world's most important energy corridors.The waterway has remained at the centre of the conflict since the war began on February 28, with disruptions to shipping sending oil prices higher and putting pressure on the global economy. Around a fifth of the world's traded oil and natural gas previously passed through the strait.Despite the diplomatic momentum, tensions across the region remain high. Iranian-backed Houthi rebels claimed fresh missile attacks on Saudi-linked shipping in the Red Sea, while fighting also threatened to flare again along the Israel-Lebanon border.
Article Summary: Us president donald trump said the united states was on the verge of launching what he described as the "biggest attack since world war ii" on iran. He claimed that the prospect of a massive military strike pushed iran back to the negotiating table.

Article Title: Vance over Rubio for 2028? What Trump reportedly told donors at private meeting
Article Text:
What Trump told donors at private meeting in White House

How midterms hold the key

Where Rubio stands

(With ANI inputs)

US President Donald Trump told donors at a private meeting that "we need to elect JD," weighing in on Vice President JD Vance as the Republican Party's presidential candidate for the 2028 election, according to The Washington Post.The remarks were reportedly made during a meeting at the White House around two weeks ago."At the end of the day, we need to elect JD," Trump said, according to two people with knowledge of the comments who spoke on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to discuss the matter.However, the report also noted that Trump's remark does not mean he has settled on a preferred candidate, as he continues to weigh both Vance and secretary of state Marco Rubio "Anyone assuming it's a lock is just getting way ahead of themselves, or just doesn't know the president very well," an official was quoted as saying.As a two-term president, Trump is constitutionally barred from seeking another term. However, he has repeatedly spoken about "running" for a third term.Vance, meanwhile, has not confirmed his plans. People who have spoken to him about the matter told The Washington Post earlier this year that he had not yet made a decision.One person close to him said the vice president would put off any decision until after the birth of his fourth child, who was born on July 19.In June, Vance told CBS News that he would discuss the matter with his wife Usha after the midterm elections but had "no doubt that the president of the United States is going to be very supportive" of whatever decision he makes. He has repeatedly maintained that he is focused on his current role and is "good friends" with Rubio.The report added that the prospect of a succession battle has already created tensions within the Republican Party, with donors, activists and party figures lining up for or against Vance.It noted that much depends on the midterm elections. A poor Republican performance could encourage challengers to contest Trump's preferred candidate and criticise his administration. Both Vance and Rubio could face intraparty attacks that Republicans would be unlikely to direct at Trump himself.According to The Washington Post, Rubio had the backing of many pre-Trump Republican donors during the 2024 vice-presidential selection process, while Vance drew support from the younger MAGA coalition that helped return Trump to power in 2024. As vice president, Vance has also cultivated ties with party donors to raise funds for the GOP.The report also noted that Rubio avoids discussing the 2028 race and has recently reduced his media appearances to avoid questions about it, according to a person close to him. However, his media team briefly fuelled speculation earlier this year by releasing a widely shared video of him delivering a campaign-style monologue during a press briefing.In internal conversations, Rubio has indicated that he intends to serve out his term, the person added. He does not have a campaign organisation in place.The report also quoted a Trump adviser as saying that the president would like to see Vance-Rubio joint ticket and regularly praises the secretary of state. However, it remains unclear whether Rubio would be willing to serve as Vance's running mate.

The remarks were reportedly made during a meeting at the white house around two weeks ago. As a two-term president, trump is constitutionally barred from seeking another term.

Article Title: Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif arrives in Saudi Arabia, pushes defence ties amid West Asia escalation
Article Text:
The trip follows Saudi Arabia’s proposal last week for a Multinational Maritime Defence Coalition

Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif arrived in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, on Thursday for a three-day official visit, accompanied by Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir and a high-level delegation, as Islamabad seeks to reinforce its strategic partnership with Riyadh amid escalating tensions across West Asia and the Gulf region.Sharif was received at King Abdulaziz International Airport by Prince Saud bin Mishaal bin Abdulaziz, Deputy Governor of the Makkah Region, along with other senior Saudi officials.The delegation includes Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar and Special Assistant Tariq Fatemi. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, who concluded a visit to Jordan earlier this week, is expected to join the delegation in Saudi Arabia.The visit comes as the conflict in West Asia has widened across multiple fronts, including the Red Sea and the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, prompting Gulf states to strengthen regional security coordination and safeguard vital maritime routes and energy supply corridors.During the August 6 to 8 visit, Sharif is scheduled to meet Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman. According to Pakistan’s Foreign Office (FO), the discussions will focus on strengthening bilateral ties and coordinating on regional and international issues.“During the visit, the prime minister will meet Crown Prince and Prime Minister of Saudi Arabia Mohammed bin Salman. Discussions would focus on consolidating the Pakistan-Saudi bilateral relationship and exchange views on areas of regional and international developments of mutual interests,” the FO said in a statement.The FO described the visit as a reflection of Pakistan’s long-standing partnership with Saudi Arabia, built on decades of mutual trust, cooperation and brotherhood.“Although taking place amid heightened tensions in the Gulf, the visit carries significance beyond the immediate crisis and short-term considerations. It will further strengthen bilateral relations, deepen strategic cooperation, enhance coordination on regional and international issues of mutual interest and also reinforce multilateral cooperation,” the FO said.The trip follows Saudi Arabia’s proposal last week for a Multinational Maritime Defence Coalition aimed at protecting commercial shipping lanes and critical energy routes through the Red Sea and the Bab al-Mandeb Strait after attacks on Saudi-linked vessels by Iran-backed Houthi forces in Yemen. Fourteen countries, including Pakistan, expressed support for the initiative.Islamabad also reiterated its commitment to Saudi Arabia’s security and emphasised the importance of ensuring the uninterrupted flow of lawful maritime commerce through the Red Sea and the Bab al-Mandeb.Pakistan and Saudi Arabia further strengthened their defence relationship last year by signing a Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement, which became operational earlier this year. Under the framework, Pakistan has deployed military personnel and aircraft to Saudi Arabia for joint training, defence cooperation and support for the kingdom’s security requirements.The visit also comes shortly after Pakistan said it was “doing its utmost” to bring the United States and Iran back to the negotiating table under the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding signed on 18 June, highlighting Islamabad’s attempt to balance its close ties with Riyadh while maintaining communication channels with Tehran.Saudi Arabia remains a key financial partner for Pakistan. According to a provisional foreign economic assistance report by Pakistan’s Ministry of Economic Affairs, Riyadh extended a fresh USD 3 billion deposit facility and rolled over an existing USD 5 billion facility for another three years in the 2025-26 financial year, providing critical support to Pakistan’s economy.
Article Summary: Pakistan prime minister shehbaz sharif arrived in jeddah, saudi arabia, on thursday for a three-day official visit. He is accompanied by chief of defence forces field marshal asim munir and a high-level delegation. Visit comes as the conflict in west asia has widened across multiple fronts, including the red sea and the bab al-mandeb strait.

Article Title: D4vd murder case: Prosecutors detail final hours of Celeste Rivas Hernandez before streamer's arrest
Article Text:
Prosecutors have outlined new allegations in the murder case against singer d4vd, claiming a heated argument with 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez preceded her death in April 2025. Court filings allege the singer killed and later dismembered the teenager before concealing her remains in his Tesla. d4vd has pleaded not guilty to all charges, and his legal team maintains he neither killed Celeste nor caused her death.

Prosecutors allege relationship breakdown led to Celeste Rivas Hernandez's death

d4vd murder investigation details evidence presented by prosecutors

The murder case against singer D4vd has taken another grim turn after prosecutors released new details describing the final hours of 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez's life. Court filings outline an alleged chain of events that began with a heated confrontation and ended in a crime prosecutors describe as carefully planned. The allegations remain unproven, and d4vd, whose legal name is David Anthony Burke, has pleaded not guilty to all charges.According to prosecutors, tensions between d4vd and Celeste reached a breaking point on April 22, 2025. Investigators say text messages recovered during the investigation suggest the teenager had become increasingly upset over the nature of their relationship and believed the singer had led her to expect a future together.The prosecution alleges that during their final argument, Celeste threatened to reveal information about their relationship that could damage the artist's rapidly growing career. At the time, d4vd was preparing to release his debut studio albumand had secured major endorsement deals while his popularity continued to rise.Court documents claim the following night, the singer arranged for an Uber to bring Celeste from her home in Lake Elsinore to his Hollywood Hills residence.The prosecution alleges:"Knowing he had to silence the victim before she ruined his music career as she had threatened, very soon after her arrival at his home, defendant stabbed the victim to death multiple times and stood by while she bled out."These allegations have not been proven in court, and the defense continues to deny that Burke was responsible for Celeste's death.Investigators claim the days following the alleged killing involved a series of purchases intended to conceal the crime. According to court filings, prosecutors allege d4vd ordered two chainsaws, a body bag, heavy-duty garbage bags, and a blue inflatable pool through Amazon The filing further claims the inflatable pool was used during the alleged dismemberment to prevent blood from spilling onto the garage floor. Prosecutors also state that forensic experts matched blue plastic fragments found with Celeste's remains to the inflatable pool recovered during the investigation.Authorities further allege that Celeste's remains were placed inside the front trunk of d4vd's Tesla, where they remained for months. Prosecutors claim the singer later parked the vehicle near his home before leaving on an international concert tour.The remains were discovered on September 8, 2025, one day after what would have been Celeste's 15th birthday. Medical officials reported that her body was in an advanced state of decomposition when it was recovered.Investigators also allege the singer repeatedly offered explanations for a strong odor noticed by people around his home and vehicle while the remains were still inside the car.Burke was arrested in April 2026 and has pleaded not guilty to charges including first-degree murder with special circumstances, continuous sexual abuse of a child under 14, and mutilating human remains. His attorney has maintained that the evidence will ultimately show he neither murdered Celeste nor caused her death.Meanwhile, Celeste's family continues to mourn the loss of the teenager. Their attorney described the emotional toll the case has taken, saying:"There are no words to express the indescribable pain the family is experiencing right now. They still have bills to pay and jobs they go to every day. All they want is time to grieve and heal."The criminal proceedings remain ongoing, and the allegations outlined by prosecutors have yet to be tested before a jury.
Article Summary: Prosecutors allege relationship breakdown led to celeste rivas hernandez's death. Court filings allege the singer killed and later dismembered the teenager before concealing her remains in his tesla. D4vd has pleaded not guilty to all charges, and his legal team maintains he neither killed celeste nor caused her death.

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Saturday lauded National Security Advisor (NSA) Ajit Doval for his contribution to India's national security and foreign policy, saying the veteran intelligence officer has played a crucial role behind every major national security decision taken by Prime Minister Narendra Modi since 2014.Speaking at a function in Pune after presenting the Lokmanya Tilak National Award 2026 to Doval, Shah said the NSA's advice and strategic inputs have been instrumental in strengthening India's security architecture and defence preparedness.He also said Doval's contribution to India's internal and external security had been so significant that history would reserve "a golden page" for him."NSA Ajit Doval has played a great role in strengthening India's foreign policy. In every decision of PM Modi for national security, Doval has had a 'role and advice' in the background," Shah said."Whenever history is written, if anyone analyses internal security and external security, then clearly, for Ajit Doval ji, a golden page will have to be kept reserved; there is no doubt about this," he added.Shah said one of the first decisions taken by PM Modi after assuming office in 2014 was appointing Doval as the National Security Advisor, a move he said transformed India's strategic posture."Today, India's foreign policy has become a foreign policy with a backbone of steel; no one can deny this. We have, along with self-respect, strengthened our position in the world," Shah said.Praising Doval's decades-long career in the Intelligence Bureau, Shah said India has emerged as a stronger and more confident nation under Modi's leadership, with Doval making a significant contribution to that transformation."After becoming NSA in 2014, Doval helped implement many strategic ideas on the ground and played a major role in modernising India's armed forces, strengthening technology, enhancing operational capability and improving the country's defence preparedness," Shah said.He added that the Modi government has fundamentally transformed both the defensive and offensive capabilities of the armed forces over the past 12 years, with Doval playing a key role in the process.Shah also noted that much of Doval's contribution can never be made public because of the confidential nature of intelligence operations.Recalling his tenure as Gujarat's home minister, Shah narrated how he first interacted with Doval following the Ahmedabad serial bomb blasts. He said then chief minister Narendra Modi had advised Gujarat Police to consult Doval while investigating the attacks."I remember Ajit ji had come to my house. The tips he gave resulted in Gujarat Police resolving not just the Ahmedabad bomb blast, but 13 bomb blasts across the country all at once. This was a very great achievement," Shah said.The Union home minister also paid tribute to Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak, calling him one of the foremost architects of India's freedom movement.He said Tilak's iconic slogan, "Swarajya is my birthright, and I shall have it," gave a new direction to India's freedom struggle and inspired generations of freedom fighters.Shah added that the slogan made Indians realise that self-rule was their right and not a favour bestowed by anyone.Describing Tilak as a fearless journalist, Shah said one could truly understand courage in journalism only by reading the articles published in Kesari, the newspaper founded by the freedom fighter."How fearless a journalist can be can only be experienced by reading the articles of Kesari," he said.Referring to Tilak's role in mobilising people through the public Ganesh and Shivaji festivals, Shah said they laid the foundation for cultural nationalism and that India continues to follow the path envisioned by the freedom fighter."India is now moving firmly on the path of cultural nationalism laid down by Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and no one can reverse that journey," he said.Shah further added that Tilak's ideas on nationalism, self-rule and social awakening continue to guide the country and remain relevant for nation-building, particularly for the younger generation.Shah said honours such as the Lokmanya Tilak National Award are not merely ceremonial but recognise those who dedicate their lives to the country and inspire future generations."When such individuals are honoured, the feeling of gratitude of society towards them is discharged... Today, the Tilak Award that has been conferred upon Ajit Doval ji... for those who live for this country and work for this country, it will become a place of great inspiration," he said.Accepting the Lokmanya Tilak National Award, Doval thanked the organisers and said he was honoured to receive an award named after Lokmanya Tilak."I am thankful for this award named after Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak and accept it with humility," Doval said.Doval also praised the country's leadership, saying, "We are very fortunate to have leaders like PM Modi and Amit Shah".
Article Summary: Amit shah presented lokmanya tilak award to ajit doval and hailed his role in india's national security. Shah said the nsa's advice and strategic inputs have been instrumental in strengthening india's security architecture and defence preparedness.

Article Title: US makes $20,000 visa bond programme permanent; India not on 50-country list
Article Text:
India not on list

Who will be affected?

The US State Department has decided to make its visa bond programme permanent after successfully running it as a pilot scheme, expanding a policy aimed at reducing visa overstays. The programme currently applies to citizens of 50 countries.Under the new rule, consular officers may require certain applicants for US visitor visas to post a bond of up to $20,000 before a visa is issued. The regulation takes effect on August 3, when it is scheduled to be published in the Federal Register. US officials have indicated that additional countries could be added to the programme in the future, Reuters cites.The visa bond programme currently covers citizens of 50 countries, including Bangladesh, Nepal and Bhutan, but India is not among them. This means Indian applicants for B-1 (business) and B-2 (tourist) visas are not affected by the new rule at present.However, the State Department has indicated that more countries could be added to the programme in the future.The rule applies to applicants seeking B-1 (business) and B-2 (tourism) visas from countries covered under the programme.According to the Federal Register notice, "Consular officers may require covered nonimmigrant visa applicants to post a bond of up to $20,000 as a condition of visa issuance, as determined by the consular officers."The State Department said a year-long review of the pilot programme found that visa bonds were effective in encouraging travellers to comply with the terms of their stay in the United States.During the pilot programme launched in 2025, consular officers could require visa applicants to post bonds of $5,000, $10,000 or $15,000.Under the permanent rule, the $5,000 option has been removed and the maximum bond amount has been increased to $20,000.Immigration and rights advocates have criticised the policy, arguing that requiring applicants to deposit thousands of dollars could discourage legitimate travel to the United States.The visa bond programme is part of a broader immigration crackdown under President Donald Trump.
Article Summary: The us state department has decided to make its visa bond programme permanent. The policy is aimed at reducing visa overstays. It currently covers citizens of 50 countries, including bangladesh, nepal and bhutan. India is not on the list of countries covered by the programme.
